findings.book_entry: To obey because it is the truth — an obedient response, not bare assent; the opposite of “believe” is apeitheō, to disobey.

anthropic.adjudicated_core_identification: To believe, in Scripture, is an obedient response to the truth rather than bare intellectual assent; its scriptural opposite is not doubt but disobedience (apeitheo), as the Greek of John 3:36 and the obeyed/believed parallel of Romans 10:16 show.

findings.book_entry: Faithfulness — obedience held steady by hope in the promise; “faith without works is dead”.

anthropic.adjudicated_core_identification: Biblical 'faith' (emunah/pistis) denotes faithfulness: steadfast obedience to God's commandments held constant in hope of the unseen promise — an enacted covenant loyalty, not a mental state of assent or bare inner trust of which works are only a downstream effect.

findings.book_entry: Covenant relationship proven by obedience — the intimate “knew” of marriage; a stranger is one not known.

openai.adjudicated_core_identification: To know God is to stand in a covenant relationship with him, a relationship whose reality is demonstrated by obedience to his commandments.

anthropic.adjudicated_core_identification: 'To know' (God, or be known by Him) denotes a covenant relationship — of the intimate, marital kind first instanced in Genesis 4:1 — whose existence is proven by keeping the commandments; to be 'not known' is to be a stranger, one outside the covenant household.

xai.adjudicated_core_identification: Knowing God is a covenant relationship (intimate like marriage) proven by obedience; the unknown are strangers/workers of lawlessness.

findings.book_entry: Keeping the commandments — “this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments”.

anthropic.adjudicated_core_identification: In Scripture's own usage, the love of God (humanity's love toward God, and love of neighbor under Him) is enacted commandment-keeping — obedience to what God commanded — rather than an inner feeling or mere affection: 'this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments' (1 John 5:3).

xai.adjudicated_core_identification: Love (the love of God) is the keeping of His commandments.
